description:
Build the four-matrix batched single-word $\mathbb{F}_3$ permanent path that the kernel crate's batched arithmetic type was introduced for, and demonstrate it agrees with the scalar kernel matrix for matrix.

## Background

The AVX2 single-word $\mathbb{F}_3$ permanent kernel zero-pads one bipedal word into a four-element lane, so three lanes of four carry no data and the kernel runs slower than the scalar one — a committed cross-CPU receipt puts scalar at $0.317$–$0.319$ of the AVX2 time at $n \in \{16, 20, 24\}$.

The module documentation states the intended resolution explicitly: the AVX2 single-word kernel exists to exercise dispatch wiring and kernel correctness on real hardware, and "the batched multi-matrix path is the performance-oriented user". That user does not exist. The batched four-lane arithmetic type it refers to landed in the kernel crate as `Bipedal3x4` (`crates/gf2-kernels-simd/src/bipedal/bipedal3.rs:183`), and nothing in the algebra crate evaluates four matrices' permanents through it. Building it makes the AVX2 lanes carry four matrices instead of one, which is what the hardware was there for.

The placement is settled here, not by the implementer: the batched Gray-walk evaluation over `Bipedal3x4` is SIMD `unsafe` and therefore lands in the kernel crate beside the existing AVX2 permanent kernel (`crates/gf2-kernels-simd/src/x86/bipedal_avx2.rs`), per `@/inv/unsafe-kernel-isolation`; the algebra crate adds only the safe public entry point and packing glue over it.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A public entry point evaluates four $\mathbb{F}_3$ permanents at once through the batched bipedal type, returning one value per input matrix in input order.
- [hard] REQ-02: The batched path agrees with the scalar single-word kernel on a randomised conformance set covering each size where one bipedal word suffices, and on the committed computer-algebra reference vectors.
- [hard] REQ-03: A batch containing fewer than four matrices returns correct values for the matrices present, with a test covering each partial-batch width.
- [hard] REQ-04: The batched path joins the crate's shared permanent behavioural suite, so it is exercised by the same contract as every other permanent backend rather than by a private test set.
- [hard] REQ-05: Each modified SIMD source file has its sibling assembly artefact regenerated in the same change.
- [hard] REQ-06: The entry point is reachable on hosts without AVX2 through the crate's existing feature and runtime-detection conventions, with a test asserting the fallback returns the same values.

## Notes

This change adds a capability and asserts its correctness. Which path the public single-matrix dispatcher selects, and the prose and benchmark labels describing that selection, are a separate concern from whether the batched path exists and is correct.
title: Four-matrix batched AVX2 single-word path for $\mathbb{F}_3$ permanents
